decisionTitle: Convert signature resolved to (category string, value float64, from, to string); equal-unit shortcut still validates the unit code against the category
rationale: Task text gave the placeholder signature `Convert(category, value, from, to string) (float64, error)` but explicitly said to reconcile it against the actual length/mass/temperature converter signatures (task 5-7 source of truth: `Convert(value float64, from, to string) (float64, error)`, confirmed in architecture.md). Implemented internal/convert/convert.go as `func Convert(category string, value float64, from, to string) (float64, error)`, dispatching via a `map[string]func(float64, string, string) (float64, error)` keyed by units.CategoryLength/Mass/Temperature, lower-casing category defensively even though the CLI layer (internal/cli) already normalizes case before calling into the domain layer. Unknown category returns apperr.NewInputError before any other check. For the FR-5 equal-unit case (from == to, compared case-insensitively via strings.EqualFold), Convert returns the input value unchanged without calling the underlying converter, avoiding the float rounding that `value*factor/factor` could introduce; per FR-18 an unknown unit code must still be an input error even when from==to, so this shortcut still checks `units.Lookup(category, from)` before returning — this is a value-identity check, not the range/rounding validation task point 5 says belongs to the sub-converters, so it does not duplicate their responsibility. Wrote internal/convert/convert_test.go covering: routing to each of the three converters, category case-insensitivity, unknown-category error, propagation of a sub-converter's own error (unknown unit on a non-equal pair), the from==to shortcut for all three categories plus a unit-case-insensitive variant, and the two edge cases of unknown unit / unknown category combined with from==to. No Go toolchain was preinstalled in this environment; installed `golang-go` (go1.19.8) via apt, same as task 5's approach, to run `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...`. Full repo build and test suite (9 packages, including internal/cli which required no code changes) pass cleanly; `go build -o /tmp/unitconv ./cmd/unitconv` also succeeds.
